paper_metadata.title: A quantum neural network with built-in self-attention mechanism

experiments.description: QNN-SAMo and QNN-SAMb evaluated on meteorological indicator forecasting for three time series (atmospheric pressure, temperature, relative humidity) using the preceding four days to predict the fifth day, plus a scalability study over sequence lengths 2-5 for QNN-SAMo.

algorithm.variant: QNN-SAMo / QNN-SAMb self-attention quantum neural network
algorithm.ansatz: Ue encoding circuit, U1 similarity ansatz, U2 attention allocation ansatz, U3 output ansatz; hardware-efficient two-qubit gate blocks

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Numerical values from the preceding days are encoded with a single Rx gate per input value; for meteorological data, the first three differenced values are used to predict the fourth, and the model forecasts the fifth day from the preceding four days.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize mean squared error between predicted and true meteorological indicator values.

problem_instance.description: Forecast atmospheric pressure, temperature, and relative humidity from historical daily sequences.
problem_instance.time_steps: 4-day input window to predict day 5; scalability study uses sequence lengths 2, 3, 4, and 5
problem_instance.dataset_size: 800 training and 200 test points per indicator; scalability study uses 794-797 training samples
problem_instance.dataset_name: China Meteorological Data Service Center dataset

dataset_specification.description: Three indicators: atmospheric pressure, temperature, relative humidity. Data were differenced and normalized. For the main task, three previous differencing points were used to predict the fourth; for the reported forecasting task, the model predicts the fifth day from the preceding four days. Evaluation repeated five times with random initialization.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: QNN-SAMo: 8 total for the main 4-day task; QNN-SAMb: 8 total for the main 4-day task; scalability study QNN-SAMo: 4, 6, 8, 10 depending on sequence length
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: QNN-SAMo: 96; QNN-SAMb: 112; scalability study QNN-SAMo: 28, 69, 96, 135 for sequence lengths 2, 3, 4, 5
quantum_resources.num_variational_params: QNN-SAMo: 136 before weight sharing, 34 after weight sharing; QNN-SAMb: 152 before weight sharing, 35 after weight sharing; scalability study QNN-SAMo: 36, 78, 136, 210 before weight sharing and 18, 26, 34, 42 after weight sharing

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Differencing and normalization of meteorological time series; sequence alignment using previous differencing points.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Prediction accuracy computed from relative error; mean and standard deviation reported over five repetitions.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports parameter reduction and improved accuracy, but does not claim a formal computational speedup for this experiment.

experiments.description: QNN-SAMo and QNN-SAMb evaluated on binary text classification for the MC and RP synthetic datasets.

algorithm.variant: QNN-SAMo / QNN-SAMb self-attention quantum neural network for text classification
algorithm.ansatz: Ue word-embedding encoding circuit, U1 similarity ansatz, U2 attention allocation ansatz, U3 output ansatz; hardware-efficient two-qubit gate blocks

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Words are embedded using parameterized encoding circuits; the paper states that six parameters are used for MC word embedding and twelve parameters for RP word embedding.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize binary cross-entropy for classifying sentences as food vs IT (MC) or subject-relative-clause vs object-relative-clause (RP).

problem_instance.description: Binary text classification on two public synthetic datasets: MC and RP.
problem_instance.num_features: MC: 17-word vocabulary; RP: 115-word vocabulary; each sentence has 3-4 words, and the model uses 4-word sentence structure in the circuit description
problem_instance.dataset_size: MC: 130 sentences total (70 train, 30 validation, 30 test); RP: 105 noun phrases total (74 train, 31 test)

dataset_specification.description: MC classifies food vs IT; RP classifies subject relative clause vs object relative clause. RP vocabulary includes 52 words only in training, 19 only in test, and 46 shared words. Evaluation repeated five times with random initialization.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: MC/RP main setup: 8 total qubits for U2 and U3; U1 uses 4 qubits in QNN-SAMo and 6 qubits in QNN-SAMb
quantum_resources.num_variational_params: QNN-SAMo: 34 after weight sharing; QNN-SAMb: 35 after weight sharing

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Word vectors are used as inputs; the paper notes that parameterized encoders can be substituted by pre-existing word embeddings.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classification metrics reported: accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score; mean and standard deviation over five repetitions.

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit speedup claim is made; the paper emphasizes accuracy and parameter efficiency.

experiments.description: QNN-SAMo and QNN-SAMb evaluated on stock closing-price prediction for 12 real-market stocks using the previous four trading days to predict the next day.

algorithm.variant: QNN-SAMo / QNN-SAMb self-attention quantum neural network for stock price prediction
algorithm.ansatz: Ue encoding circuit, U1 similarity ansatz, U2 attention allocation ansatz, U3 output ansatz; hardware-efficient two-qubit gate blocks

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each of the four preceding days is encoded with a single Rx rotation gate; input features are normalized to [0,1] using min-max normalization.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize mean squared error for next-day closing price prediction.

problem_instance.description: Predict next-day closing prices for 12 stocks from Yahoo Finance.
problem_instance.time_steps: 4-day input window to predict the next day

dataset_specification.description: Tickers: AAPL, AMGN, BA, CAT, CSCO, HD, IBM, JNJ, JPM, KO, MMM, MSFT. Each day includes opening price, highest price, lowest price, closing price, adjusted closing price, and trading volume. Initial 80% of each sequence used for training and remaining 20% for testing.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: 8 total for U2 and U3; U1 uses 2 qubits in QNN-SAMo and 3 qubits in QNN-SAMb
quantum_resources.num_variational_params: QNN-SAMo: 34 after weight sharing; QNN-SAMb: 35 after weight sharing

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Min-max normalization of each input entry to [0,1].
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Evaluation with R2, MAPE, and RMSE; results reported per stock.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports predictive performance improvements over SAM, but no explicit speedup factor or runtime comparison is given.

experiments.description: Robustness evaluation of QNN-SAMo under five common quantum noise channels on meteorological forecasting, text classification, and stock-related settings.

algorithm.ansatz: Same QNN-SAMo circuit as in the main experiments; noise applied to the U3 layer

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Noise is injected into the eight qubits of the U3 layer after the same encoding and attention pipeline used in the main tasks.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Task-dependent objective from the underlying experiment; robustness measured by test accuracy under noise.

problem_instance.description: Noise robustness tested on meteorological indicators, MC text classification, and RP text classification; the paper reports the noisy results in a combined table.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Meteorological dataset, MC dataset, RP dataset

dataset_specification.description: Noise channels applied during training/evaluation to the U3 layer; accuracy reported for p = 0, 0.005, 0.01, and 0.05 depending on channel.

noise_model.mitigation_details: The paper discusses ZNE for depolarizing and bit-flip noise and randomized compilation as mitigation ideas, but does not report applying them in the experiments.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Accuracy compared across noise levels; mean and standard deviation over five repetitions.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper discusses robustness under noise and mitigation ideas, but does not report a speedup claim.
